author: Good Enough
description:
Patients were locked alone in isolation cells, and some began throwing themselves into the walls.

In early insane asylums, padded rooms and long-term isolation were used as “treatment,” often leaving patients restrained in straightjackets with no escape for hours or even days.

This video explores one of the most disturbing practices in asylum history, how it was justified at the time, and what patients were forced to endure inside these institutions.
